newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares battered by profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares battered by profit-taking.

text.p: Profit-taking dashed hopes of a Danish share rally on Thursday, sending prices back down after an initial rise, and dealers saw no prospect of a reverse on Friday.
"It's primarily profit-taking that's sending shares down and sentiment is a bit lukewarm. It all points to falling prices on Friday," a dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index fell 0.36 point to 126.87 in overall bourse turnover of 687 million crowns. The KFX December future fell 0.65 point to 127.15, with 200 contracts, each worth 100,000 crowns, traded.

The major banks continued to suffer from Wednesday's downgrading by Capel; Unibank fell a further two crowns after its three percent loss yesterday and Den Danske Bank sagged 0.76 crown to 423.24. BG Bank was untraded at 253 crowns.
Tele Danmark, swept along in the wake of Deutsche Telekom's mammoth offering, swung between 293 and 298 crowns before settling at 296, 0.06 crown down from Wednesday's close.

The dealer saw the share as steady for another day or two before rising again. Also seen on the rise was Danisco, which dealers believed may have bottomed out at 335 crowns after falling three. --Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
